sentences.text: This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the appellants/claimants arising out of the award dated 31/03/2022 passed by Seventh Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (hereinafter referred as "Claims Tribunal), District- Morena (M.P.) in Claim Case No.265/2019 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Seventh Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute, however, the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard is not in question.
3.

As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of death of Banti @ Feran Singh due to motor accident, Claims Tribunal has awarded NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27869 2 MA-3046-2022 compensation to the tune of Rs. 14,04,712/- with interest from the date of filing of claim application till its realization.
4. Counsel for appellants/claimants submitted that impugned Award passed by the Claims Tribunal without considering appreciation of law and the fact.
It is further submitted that Claims Tribunal wrongly assessed income of the deceased without considering whole aspect of the case, passed the impugned award.

It is also submitted that according to pay-slip (Ex.P.21), deceased was working as a Manager in wine shop and earned Rs. 15,000/- per month with additional allowance i.e. Rs.
Smt. Guddan vs Vishnu Singh Tomar on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162381814/
1 5000/- but Claims Tribunal without considering pay certificate (Ex.P.21) assessed income of deceased as Skilled labour under the Minimum Wages Act.
It is also submitted that deceased has agricultural land and also earned Rs. 5000/- per month from the agricultural land, therefore, his income should be assessed Rs. 20,000/- per month.

It is further contended that Claims Tribunal has not awarded compensation under the head of future prospect and loss of consortium, as per the verdict of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur and others reported in 2020 ACJ 2131.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

Counsel for appellants/claimants relied upon the case of Rasmita Biswal and Ors. Vs Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Ltd and An r. 2021 Supreme (SC)805 and also coordinate Bench Gwalior in M.A. No. 252/2014 (The New India Insurance Co.
Ltd Vs Smt. Reena) order dated 26/07/2022.

sentences.text: Hence, it is prayed that reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded to the claimants.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:27869 3 MA-3046-2022 Company contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and argued in support of the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal.
6.
Heard the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and perused the impugned Award.

7. It is submitted by counsel for appellants/claimants that deceased was working as a Manager in wine shop and earned Rs. 15,000/- per month with additional allowance of Rs. 5000/- and he filed pay certificate (Ex.P.21) which was issued by Chandrapal Singh Sikarwar (A.W.3) who deposed before the Tribunal that deceased was working as a Manager in wine shop last five years.
He also used to pay salary i.e. Rs. 15,000/- per month with additional allowance of Rs. 5000/- per month and he issued Pay certificate (Ex.P.21).

8. In cross-examination, Chandrapal Singh Sikarwar (A.W.3) admitted that he maintains all documents in regard to his business but he is unable to adduce any substantial documents that he used to pay Rs. 15,000/- as salary to the deceased.
He had not adduced any register in which it was mentioned that Chandrapal Singh Sikarwar (A.W.3) gave regularly Rs. 15,000/- to the deceased.

9. In the case of Rasmita Biswal and Ors. Vs Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Ltd (Supra), the Apex Court relied upon Ex.P.8 which was issued by (A.W.3) which shows that deceased was Supervisor in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27869 4 MA-3046-2022 Organization and his salary was Rs. 15,000/- per month.
10. Coordinate Bench Gwalior in M.A. No. 252/2014 (The New India Insurance Co. Ltd Vs Smt.
Reena) order dated 26/07/2022, the Coordinate Bench of this Court held that income of deceased i.e. Rs. 14,500/- was issued by Mahakal Construction Company as deceased was working as a Supervisor.
11.

2 month from wine shop.

12. In the case of LIC of India and Anrs Vs Ram Pal Singh Bisen, 2010 AIR SCW 1900, wherein the Apex Court held as under :-
"25.

entities.text: LIC of India and Anrs Vs Ram Pal Singh Bisen, 2010 AIR SCW 1900
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
No doubt, it is true that failure to prove the defence does not amount to an admission, nor does it reverse or discharge the burden of proof of the plaintiff but still the duty cast on the defendants has to be discharged by adducing oral evidence,
which the appellants have miserably failed to do.

Appellants, even though a defaulting party, committed breach and failed to carry out a legislative imposition,
then had still to convince this Court as to what was the just cause for doing the same.
Thus looking to the matter from any angle, it is fully established that appellants had miserably failed to prove and establish their defence in the case.
26.We are of the firm opinion that mere admission of document in evidence does not amount to its proof.
In other words, mere marking of exhibit on a document does not dispense with its proof, which is required to be done in accordance with law.
As has been mentioned herein above, despite perusal of the record, we have not been able to come to know as to under what circumstances respondent plaintiff had admitted those documents.

Even otherwise, his admission of those documents cannot carry the case of the appellants any further and much to the prejudice of the respondent."
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27869 5 MA-3046-2022 13.

This Court is of the considered view that appellants/claimants only filed pay certificate (Ex.P.21)
but he is unable to prove pay certificate (Ex.P.21) in accordance with law.

Therefore, mere exhibiting document (Ex.P.21), it can not be proved that deceased used to receive Rs. 15,000/- per month with additional allowance of Rs. 5000/- per month working as a Manager in wine shop.

Therefore, it is proved that claimants failed to prove that deceased was working as a Manager in wine shop and was receiving salary of Rs. 15,000/- with additional allowance of Rs. 5000/-.
14.

It is submission of counsel for appellants/claimants that claimants filed Khasra documents Ex.P.15 to Ex.P.20 before the Tribunal but Claims Tribunal did not consider income of deceased by agriculture source while deceased was owner of the agricultural land.
Therefore, Rs. 5000/- should be given under the head of agricultural head.

15. But in Ponnumany Alias Krishnan & Anr vs V.A. Mohanan & Ors, AIR 2008 SC 2014, the Apex Court held that in regard to income from agriculture, no general rule of law is applicable because successors of legal heirs received agricultural land as successors.

16. In the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Charlie And Anr. AIR 2005 SC 2157 , the Apex Court observed that income from agriculture is a normal rule/general principle about the deprivation of income is directly not applicable to the cases where agricultural income is the source of income of deceased/injured and other circumstances have to be considered because agricultural Smt. Guddan vs Vishnu Singh Tomar on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162381814/
3 land is always accrued in favour of successors(s) of the deceased.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27869 6 MA-3046-2022 17.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court is of the considered view that Claims Tribunal has not committed error in not assessing income of deceased in regard to agricultural land.
18. As earlier discussing, it is proved that appellants/claimants are unable to adduce any substantial documents in regard to income of the deceased 19.

In the case of Sukhdevi Vs Devendra Kumar, ILR 2014 M.P. 172, Kanvar Devi Vs Bansal Roadways, 2008 ACJ 2182 and National Insurance Company Ltd Vs Renu Devi, (2008) 3 ACC 134 ,
wherein it was held that claimants are unable to adduce substantial documents in regard to income of the deceased then Claims Tribunal must assess income of the deceased as per Minimum Wages Act.

sentences.text: 20. Considering all documents filed by the appellants and evaluating the evidence produced by the appellants/claimants in respect of income and lack of documentary evidence, this Court is of the considered opinion that Tribunal has not committed any error in assessing income of deceased as Rs.8160/- per month as a skilled labour which is just and proper.
Therefore, no interference is warranted in this regard.

21. L ooking to the age of the deceased, 40 percent towards future prospect ought to have applied by the Claims Tribunal in the light of decision of Supreme Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd Vs Nanu Ram @ Chuhruram and others (2018)18 SCC 130 and Satinder Kaur (Supra), therefore, claimants are entitled for future prospect at the rate of 40% and consortium.

Accordingly, claimants are entitled to get following compensation amount as under:-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:27869 7 MA-3046-2022 Heads Amount Monthly income 8,160/-PM Total Income 8160 X 12 = 97,920 PA Future prospects 39168 (40%) Income+Future prospects (97,920 + 39168 = 1,37,088)
Personal Expenses 1/5th 27,418/-
 Multiplier (17) 1,09,670 X17 = 18  Loss of consortium 40,000 X 7= 2,80,0

Other Heads (Funeral and loss of estate) 30,000/-
 Transportation Expenses 3000/-
 Total Rs.21,77,390 22.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.21,77,390/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.14,04,712/-.

Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Smt. Guddan vs Vishnu Singh Tomar on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162381814/
4 Rs.7,72,678/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
23.

The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.

24. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal,
the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants- claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.

Thereafter, the Registry NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:27869 8 MA-3046-2022 shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
